title: Payments on Independent Living Accounts — Accepted Methods, Card Convenience Fee and Returned Payments
content:
## Accepted methods

Payments on an Independent Living Residency Agreement account are accepted by ACH autopay, one-time ACH, personal check, certified check, credit card or debit card, and each payment instrument is posted once under its own reference.

## Order of application

A payment is applied to the oldest outstanding charge first, by billing period and then by posting date.

## Card convenience fee

A credit card payment carries a card convenience fee of the card convenience percentage of the apartment type, applied to the payment amount, rounded to the cent half up and referencing the card payment entry. Debit cards, ACH and checks carry no fee.

| Payment method | Convenience fee |
|---|---|
| Credit card | Card convenience percentage of the payment amount, rounded to the cent half up |
| Debit card | None |
| ACH autopay or one-time ACH | None |
| Personal check or certified check | None |

Hypothetical example: a credit card payment of 2,345.67 at a convenience percentage of 2.9 carries a fee of 68.02443, rounded half up to 68.02.

## Returned payments

When the bank returns a payment, the returned amount is reinstated referencing the returned payment entry, and a returned payment fee of the apartment type's returned payment fee is charged referencing the same entry. A payment is returned at most once: the reinstatement and the fee each reference the one returned payment entry.

## Certified funds restriction

Once the number of returned payments posted on the residency within the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date reaches the returned-payment limit of the apartment type, further payments on the residency are accepted only by certified check or ACH autopay until 365 days have passed since the latest return.

| Returned payments in the rolling 365 days | Payment methods accepted |
|---|---|
| Below the returned-payment limit | Every accepted method |
| At or above the limit | Certified check or ACH autopay only, until 365 days have passed since the latest return |

## Status of the account

Payments may be posted while the residency is in active, notice given or vacated status; a payment toward a reservation is taken as the reservation deposit instead.

## Points of judgement

- **Is a returned payment counted by the date of the original payment or the date of the return?** The count reads the returned payment entries posted within the rolling 365 days ending on the handling date.
- **Does a payment on a vacated residency post?** Yes; payments may be posted while the residency is active, notice given or vacated.
